title: How MRI Works | Science Behind Magnetic Resonance Imaging
tags: pale blue thoughts miracles of science
description:
MRI, or Magnetic Resonance Imaging, is one of the most fascinating medical technologies ever invented. Unlike X-rays and CT scans, MRI does not use ionizing radiation. Instead, it uses magnetic fields and radio waves to take detailed pictures of your body — completely safely.

In this episode of Miracles of Science, Pale Blue Thoughts breaks down exactly how MRI works. Since our bodies are 70% water, and water is full of hydrogen atoms, MRI machines exploit the magnetic spin of hydrogen protons. Place the body in a strong magnetic field, apply radio waves, and you can manipulate these tiny “atomic compasses.” When they relax back into position, they release energy that the machine converts into stunning 2D and 3D images .

We’ll explain concepts like the Zeeman Effect, excitation and relaxation, signal detection, and image reconstruction — all simplified so anyone can understand. You’ll also see how different tissues give different signals, creating natural contrast, and how contrast agents like gadolinium enhance visibility.

We also expose pseudoscience myths: if people think the Earth’s magnetic field affects your blood, they should try stepping inside an MRI machine 40,000 times stronger than Earth’s field. Spoiler: nothing happens!

Finally, we explore the brain’s big brother scan: fMRI (functional MRI). It maps blood flow to show which brain regions activate during tasks, or even at rest (rs-fMRI). This helps us study memory, language, brain disorders, and human cognition.

If you’ve searched for how MRI works, MRI explained simply, fMRI brain scan, MRI vs X-ray safety, or hydrogen atom MRI physics, this video has all the answers.
